items.prompt:
In a chemical reaction, substances change into:
A) The same substances
B) New substances with different properties
C) Only colder substances
D) Nothing
items.answer: B) New substances with different properties

steps: Chemical reactions form new substances with different properties.

items.prompt:
Which is a sign of a chemical reaction?
A) A color change
B) A change in location
C) A change in size only
D) Being lifted

steps: A color change is evidence a new substance formed.

items.prompt:
Ice melting into water is a:
A) Chemical reaction
B) Physical change
C) New element
D) Precipitate

steps: It is still water; no new substance forms, so it is physical.

items.prompt:
Two clear liquids are mixed and a solid settles out. This solid is called a:
A) Gas
B) Precipitate
C) Mixture
D) Melt

steps: A solid forming from a reaction is a precipitate.

items.prompt:
To decide if a chemical reaction occurred, scientists compare the substances':
A) Prices
B) Properties before and after
C) Names only
D) Owners

steps: Different properties after indicate a new substance formed.

items.prompt:
Bubbles forming when two substances mix is a sign that:
A) A solid melted
B) A gas formed
C) Nothing happened
D) The temperature stayed the same

steps: Gas production is a sign of a chemical reaction.

items.prompt:
A student mixes two substances and the properties afterward are identical to before. The best conclusion is:
A) A chemical reaction occurred
B) No new substance formed, so no chemical reaction occurred
C) A gas definitely formed
D) A precipitate formed
items.answer: B) No new substance formed, so no chemical reaction occurred

steps: Unchanged properties mean no new substance, so no reaction.

items.prompt:
Which observation would best show a chemical reaction rather than a physical change?
A) Water changing to ice
B) A new solid and a color change appearing after mixing
C) Sugar dissolving in water
D) A nail being bent
items.answer: B) A new solid and a color change appearing after mixing

steps: A new solid and color change indicate new substances formed.
